::: proof
Expand the penalized residual sum of squares:

$$
\ba
\text{PRSS}_\l(\vb)
&= \tp{\vy}\vy - \tp{\vy}\mat{B}\vb - \tp{\vb}\tp{\mat{B}}\vy
+ \tp{\vb}\tp{\mat{B}}\mat{B}\vb + \l \tp{\vb}\mat{P}\vb
&& \text{(distribute the product)}
\\ &= \tp{\vy}\vy - 2\tp{\vb}\tp{\mat{B}}\vy
+ \tp{\vb}\tp{\mat{B}}\mat{B}\vb + \l \tp{\vb}\mat{P}\vb
&& \text{(a scalar equals its transpose)}
\\ &= \tp{\vy}\vy - 2\tp{\vb}\tp{\mat{B}}\vy
+ \tp{\vb}\paren{\tp{\mat{B}}\mat{B} + \l\mat{P}}\vb
&& \text{(collect the quadratic terms)}
\ea
$$

Write $\mat{A} \eqdef \tp{\mat{B}}\mat{B} + \l\mat{P}$,
a symmetric $q \times q$ matrix.
The gradient with respect to $\vb$ is

$$
\ba
\ub{\deriv{\vb}\text{PRSS}_\l(\vb)}_{q \times 1}
&= -2\tp{\mat{B}}\vy + 2\mat{A}\vb
&& \text{(gradients of linear and symmetric quadratic forms)}
\ea
$$

Setting the gradient to $\mat{0}_{q \times 1}$ gives the penalized normal equations:

$$
\ba
-2\tp{\mat{B}}\vy + 2\mat{A}\vb &= \mat{0}_{q \times 1}
&& \text{(set the gradient to zero)}
\\ 2\mat{A}\vb &= 2\tp{\mat{B}}\vy
&& \text{(add } 2\tp{\mat{B}}\vy \text{ to both sides)}
\\ \mat{A}\vb &= \tp{\mat{B}}\vy
&& \text{(divide by 2)}
\\ \vb &= \mat{A}^{-1}\tp{\mat{B}}\vy
&& \text{(multiply on the left by } \mat{A}^{-1}\text{)}
\ea
$$

{{< slidebreak >}}

This stationary point is the unique minimizer
because the Hessian $2\mat{A}$ is positive definite:
for any $\vec{v} \ne \mat{0}_{q \times 1}$,
$\tp{\vec{v}}\mat{A}\vec{v}
= \tp{(\mat{B}\vec{v})}(\mat{B}\vec{v}) + \l \tp{\vec{v}}\mat{P}\vec{v} \ge 0$,
since both terms are nonnegative.
If equality held, then $\mat{A}\vec{v} = \mat{0}_{q \times 1}$,
because $\tp{\vec{v}}\mat{A}\vec{v} = 0$ implies $\mat{A}\vec{v} = \mat{0}_{q \times 1}$
for a positive semidefinite matrix $\mat{A}$;
that would contradict the invertibility of $\mat{A}$.
So $\tp{\vec{v}}\mat{A}\vec{v} > 0$.

Finally, the fitted values are

$$
\ba
\est{\vy}
&= \mat{B}\evb_\l
&& \text{(fitted values of a basis expansion)}
\\ &= \mat{B}\mat{A}^{-1}\tp{\mat{B}}\vy
&& \text{(substitute } \evb_\l\text{)}
\\ &= \mat{S}_\l \vy
&& \text{(definition of } \mat{S}_\l\text{)}
\ea
$$
:::

::: notes
The smoothing spline of @def-smoothing-spline is a special case.
By @rem-smoothing-spline-natural-cubic, its minimizer is a natural cubic spline,
so it can be written $g(x) = \sum_k \b_k b_k(x)$ in a natural cubic spline basis,
and its penalty is $\int g''(t)^2\,dt = \tp{\vb}\mat{P}\vb$
with $P_{jk} \eqdef \int b_j''(t)\, b_k''(t)\,dt$.
:::
